messages:
phil: heads-up — after the canary deployment (~10:30) we saw p95 spike and a burst of 429s on runtime-cluster-7. digging into the batcher traces now.
sophia: link to the p95 dashboard?
phil: https://grafana.internal/redwood/runtime/p95?panel=continuous-batcher. quick snapshot: two windows where batch assembly mixed very short (<=8) and very long (>=512) sequences so kernel chosen = wavkernel_v2 heavy path and latency jumped.
raj: that pattern rings a bell — short+long mixing causes kernel selection oscillation. the batcher should avoid wide seq variance in the same microbatch.
phil: pasting sample trace:
```
[2026-02-18T10:32:11Z] batch_id=abc123 selected_kernel=wavkernel_v2 batch_sizes=[4,28] seqs=[6,600,7,512] kv_cache_hits=0.09 latency_ms=1120
[2026-02-18T10:32:11Z] admission_reason=allowed token_budget_remaining=1800 pending_tokens=2920
[2026-02-18T10:32:11Z] response=429 count=8
```
maya: looks like admission allowed the long requests to join and token budget accounting failed to prevent oversubscription.
sophia: can we avoid hard 429s for this class? maybe soft-reject or route to cheap fallback (quantized kernel) instead of dropping.
raj: two levers i see: (A) stronger token-budget gating on the queue (reject/redirect when pending_tokens > soft_budget) (B) probabilistic early-eject for batches with high seq variance so some requests get preemptively routed out.
phil: proposal: enable token_budget_soft = 2400 tokens per queue, and runtime.admit.prob_eject_pct = 0.12 (12% probe eject) for the canary cohort. fallback_variant = quant8 for any preemptive routes.
maya: plan sounds reasonable. also add a kernel_hint in batch assembly so when seq_variance>threshold we prefer the short-tail optimized kernel for new joins.
sophia: we must add metrics before we flip flags: batch_seq_variance, kernel_mismatch_rate (selected_kernel != expected_by_profile), preemptive_routed_count, kv_cache_occupancy_window.
raj: add alert: if kernel_mismatch_rate > 0.02 and p95_latency > 800ms over 5m, page oncall.
phil: small implementation note: emit admission_reason labels: token_over_budget / seq_variance_eject / kv_pressure / fallback_route so we can slice.
ci-bot: deploy started -> canary/runtime-batcher-v3.2 -> target=10% traffic (hosts: runtime-7, runtime-9)
deploy-bot: canary health checks: passing 1/3 -> scaling to full canary
maya: experiment runbook draft:
1) Turn on flags on canary: runtime.batch.token_budget_soft=2400, runtime.admit.prob_eject_pct=0.12, runtime.admit.fallback_variant=quant8, runtime.admit.soft_429=true
2) Enable telemetry: the metrics sophia listed
3) Run for 2h, observe p95, mismatch_rate, cost_delta for quant8
4) If p95 drops >15% and mismatch_rate < baseline -> rollout; else rollback
phil: cost note: quant8 increases token throughput but may degrade output quality; we should measure any QA-eval regressions on sample prompts.
sophia: add sampling hook: log 1% of preemptive routes' request+response for offline QA checks (redact PII).
raj: also implement a fast-path in kernel selection: when variance > V, prefer kernels with short-tail optimization. flag name: runtime.batch.kernel_hint = "short_tail" for the batch assembly.
phil: PRs?
maya: i'll open two PRs: one for admission gating + metrics, one for kernel_hint + unit tests. PR titles: "admit: token-soft-budget & prob-eject + metrics" and "batcher: kernel_hint for high-variance assemblies". estimating 4h + 3h.
sophia: once PRs land, i'll wire the dash and alert, and coordinate canary flip.
phil: rollback plan: set runtime.batch.token_budget_soft back to default (influx value) or disable prob_eject_pct, and remove fallback routing. infra can cancel canary via canaryctl -> rollback runtime-batcher-v3.1
raj: tiny risk: preemptive routing may hide KV pressure signals. ensure we still record kv_cache_occupancy per-preroute so we can analyze.
sophia: good call. add kv_cache_preserved flag in telemetry so we know whether preemptive route bypassed cache.
phil: ok — i'll own rollout and preliminary analysis. tagging @sophia @raj @maya. thanks.
maya: noted. PRs incoming in ~2h.
sophia: :thumbsup:
phil: thanks everyone. I'll post a short postmortem if canary shows regression or an update after 2h.
